note: Fixture keys are throwaway values generated for these vectors and published on purpose. Never a real Kite, agent, or user key.

cases.name: deal-contract-minimal
cases.note: baseline DealContract: JCS bytes + the termsHash derived from them, with the proposer signature stripped

cases.name: deal-contract-member-order-and-stripping
cases.note: wire order is irrelevant; signatures and a declared termsHash are stripped — byte-identical to the baseline

cases.name: deal-contract-integer-members
cases.note: integer-valued members: any renumbering changes the bytes and breaks the signature

cases.name: deal-contract-unicode-escaping
cases.note: UTF-8 emitted literally; only the JSON-mandated escapes appear

cases.name: agreement-command-basic
cases.note: AgreementCommand: canonical signed bytes, with the signature member stripped

cases.name: agreement-valid-buyer
cases.note: the buyer agreementSig (§4.1): agreementId32 = keccak256(UTF-8 agreement id), amount in USDC base units, KiteFulfill domain WITHOUT verifyingContract

cases.name: agreement-valid-seller
cases.note: the seller agreementSig over the IDENTICAL digest — the accept gate verifies both

cases.name: delivery-valid-seller
cases.note: sellerDeliverySig: deliveryHash is §4.2’s sha256 content hash as raw bytes; receiptHash is the PRIOR proof anchor

cases.name: acceptance-valid-buyer
cases.note: buyerAcceptanceSig over the vault Acceptance struct

cases.name: rejection-valid-buyer
cases.note: buyerRejectionSig: reasonHash = keccak256(UTF-8 reasonCode) — the §4.2 derivation inside the signed struct

cases.name: resolution-valid-arbiter
cases.note: arbiterSig: decisionId (bytes32) = keccak256(UTF-8 decisionId string); sellerBps is a uint16 word

cases.name: appeal-valid-seller
cases.note: sellerAppealSig over the vault Appeal struct

cases.name: refund-consent-valid-seller
cases.note: sellerConsentSig over the vault RefundConsent struct

cases.name: activation-valid-buyer
cases.note: buyerActivationSig: the funding artifact (§6.2.1), under the vault domain; windows are §3.1 platform config read back via the funding interaction

cases.name: activation-valid-seller
cases.note: sellerActivationSig over the IDENTICAL Activation digest — the vault verifies the pair

cases.name: deal-contract-accepted
cases.note: the COMMITTED shape: two entries, both with agreementSig; signatures are stripped before hashing, so the termsHash is unchanged

cases.name: terms-valid-buyer
cases.note: DealContract signature: over the termsHash STRING, not its bytes

cases.name: terms-valid-seller
cases.note: the countersignature: identical termsHash, different key, different recovered address

cases.name: command-valid-seller
cases.note: AgreementCommand signature

cases.name: funding-envelope-valid-buyer
cases.note: party envelope for the funding/evidence/proofs interactions (§6.2.1)

cases.name: valid-buyer-submission
cases.note: the buyer supplies its wallet, its Activation signature, and the EIP-3009 authorization bound to expectedDealId

cases.name: valid-seller-submission
cases.note: the seller supplies only its Activation co-signature — its one funding artifact

cases.name: reject-auth3009-without-expected-deal-id
cases.note: auth3009 without expectedDealId: the authorization is bound to a vault deal id nothing can then check against dealIdFor — the deal-identity binding (§6.2.1) requires the pair

cases.name: reject-buyer-sets-seller-sig
cases.note: role binding (§6.2.1): validated as a BUYER submission, a seller co-signature is not a buyer artifact and is rejected

cases.name: reject-malformed-auth3009
cases.note: auth3009 uses snake_case wire fields; the camelCase validAfter/validBefore variant that a naive client might emit is a different, invalid object

cases.name: reject-activation-sig-bad-recovery-byte
cases.note: 65 bytes and well-formed hex, but the trailing recovery byte is 0xab. The settlement layer's SignatureChecker refuses any v outside {27,28}, and funding artifacts are write-once — accepting this would wedge the deal permanently, after the buyer's budget is committed.

cases.name: reject-malformed-expected-deal-id
cases.note: expectedDealId must be a 0x-prefixed 32-byte (64 hex) EscrowVault deal id; a short/garbage value is rejected before it can be mistaken for a real one

cases.name: reject-seller-sets-expected-deal-id
cases.note: role binding (§6.2.1): validated as a SELLER submission, the buyer-only expectedDealId is rejected

cases.name: reject-seller-sets-buyer-wallet
cases.note: role binding: validated as a SELLER submission, the buyer wallet is rejected — a counterparty able to set it can make the deal unfundable

cases.name: valid-chain
cases.note: a three-link chain: each later link quotes its predecessor, the newest proofHash is the receiptHash the next settlement signature quotes, and command identity appears only on the link an AgreementCommand drove

cases.name: reject-snake-case-spelling
cases.note: a Runtime leaking its storage spelling: the required camelCase members are absent, so a consumer reads null for the receiptHash anchor and signs nothing — the failure this schema exists to make loud

cases.name: reject-missing-proof-hash
cases.note: proofHash is what the next settlement signature quotes as receiptHash; a link without it cannot anchor anything

cases.name: reject-malformed-proof-hash
cases.note: a proof hash is a 32-byte digest in the sha256: or 0x spelling; a short value would be padded into a different anchor

cases.name: reject-sequence-zero
cases.note: the chain starts at 1: sequence 0 would make "the proof at sequence - 1" unresolvable

cases.name: reject-cross-tag-terms-as-command
cases.note: a terms signature presented as a command signature MUST NOT verify — the tags separate the families

cases.name: reject-cross-tag-command-as-terms
cases.note: and the reverse

cases.name: reject-cross-tag-funding-as-command
cases.note: the §6.2.1 funding tag is separated from the command tag too

cases.name: reject-wrong-key
cases.note: cryptographically valid, but recovers to an address the named agent does not hold

cases.name: reject-mutated-body
cases.note: body changed after signing — recovery yields an unrelated address

cases.name: reject-bare-hex-no-0x
cases.note: the profile fixes one spelling: 0x-prefixed 65-byte r‖s‖v. Bare hex is rejected, not guessed at

cases.name: reject-legacy-recovery-id
cases.note: wire v is 27/28; the raw 0/1 recovery id MUST be rejected, not silently normalized

cases.name: reject-truncated-signature
cases.note: a signature that is not exactly 65 bytes is malformed

cases.name: valid-delivered
cases.note: kite.contract.delivered: schema-valid and correctly signed by the seller

cases.name: valid-accepted
cases.note: kite.contract.accepted: schema-valid and correctly signed by the buyer

cases.name: valid-rejected
cases.note: kite.contract.rejected: schema-valid and correctly signed by the buyer

cases.name: valid-appealed
cases.note: kite.contract.appealed: schema-valid and correctly signed by the seller

cases.name: valid-refund-consented
cases.note: kite.contract.refund_consented: schema-valid and correctly signed by the seller

cases.name: valid-arbiter-decided
cases.note: kite.contract.arbiter_decided: schema-valid and correctly signed by the arbiter

cases.name: invalid-unknown-command-type
cases.note: commandType is a closed enum — an unknown type is rejected at the schema, before any state logic

cases.name: invalid-missing-payload-hash
cases.note: payloadHash is required: without it a Runtime cannot tell a swapped payload from a bad signature

cases.name: invalid-negative-revision
cases.note: expectedRevision is an integer of at least 1

cases.name: invalid-zero-revision
cases.note: expectedRevision 0 is rejected, not read as an opt-out from the concurrency check

cases.name: invalid-command-id-shape
cases.note: commandId must match ^cmd_[A-Za-z0-9]+$ — it is an idempotency key, not free text

cases.name: invalid-additional-member
cases.note: additionalProperties is false: an unknown member would sit inside the signature but outside every implementation's understanding of it

cases.name: invalid-actor-not-a-did
cases.note: actorAgentId must be a did:kite DID — a bare id cannot be resolved to a key

cases.name: invalid-terms-hash-spelling
cases.note: hash references are the sha256:<64 lowercase hex> string form throughout

cases.name: invalid-delivered-empty-payload
cases.note: the delivered payload requires evidenceId and deliveryHash — an empty payload names no artifact and cannot settle

cases.name: invalid-accepted-with-delivery-payload
cases.note: payload members are bound to their commandType: delivery members inside an accepted command are rejected, not ignored

cases.name: invalid-delivered-extra-payload-member
cases.note: additionalProperties is false inside the payload too — an unknown payload member would sit inside the signature but outside the contract

cases.name: invalid-accepted-empty-payload
cases.note: fixed_outcome/v1 settles on chain: every payload carries its settlement signature and expiry, so no payload is ever the empty object

cases.name: invalid-zero-expiry
cases.note: expiry bounds the embedded settlement signature: zero is not a bound, and the vault rejects an expired call

cases.name: conflict-idempotency-divergent-replay
cases.note: reusing a commandId with different content is a conflict, not a retry — both bodies are schema-valid

cases.name: conflict-stale-revision
cases.note: expectedRevision behind the agreement: the actor signed against a state that has since moved

cases.name: valid-command-driven
cases.note: party-command transition: commandId/commandHash present and inside the signature

cases.name: audit-restamp-keeps-signature
cases.note: the audit fields are excluded from the preimage, so a re-stamp reuses the signature — and is therefore not evidence

cases.name: valid-runtime-driven-no-command
cases.note: chain observation: commandId/commandHash omitted from the canonical object, never null

cases.name: valid-but-unsigned
cases.note: runtimeSignature: null is schema-VALID and a visible non-guarantee — distinct from receipt: null, which means no receipt at all

cases.name: reject-mutated-transition
cases.note: toState is inside the preimage: changing the transition breaks the signature

cases.name: reject-signed-by-non-runtime
cases.note: a well-formed signature from a key that is not the pinned Runtime key

cases.name: valid-invalid-command-schema
cases.note: the command failed schema validation for its declared schema/version

cases.name: valid-unsupported-extension-version
cases.note: refused before formation, so it carries no deal identity

cases.name: valid-invalid-signature
cases.note: the signature did not verify against the resolved actor key, profile and domain tag

cases.name: valid-unknown-key
cases.note: the keyId did not resolve, or was not valid at command time

cases.name: valid-runtime-key-required
cases.note: one or both Agreement signatures omitted their runtime keyId

cases.name: valid-runtime-not-found
cases.note: the selected runtime key does not resolve

cases.name: valid-runtime-pending
cases.note: the selected runtime is pending and may be retried after activation

cases.name: valid-runtime-revoked
cases.note: the selected runtime was revoked permanently

cases.name: valid-runtime-agent-mismatch
cases.note: the selected runtime belongs to a different Agent DID

cases.name: valid-runtime-signature-mismatch
cases.note: the Agreement signature does not verify under its declared runtime key

cases.name: valid-agreement-runtime-mismatch
cases.note: the request used a runtime other than the authority pinned to the Agreement

cases.name: valid-unauthorized-actor
cases.note: a genuine signature from a party that does not own this command type

cases.name: valid-unknown-deal
cases.note: dealId does not resolve, so no other context can be reported

cases.name: valid-terms-hash-mismatch
cases.note: the command's termsHash is not the accepted contract's

cases.name: valid-payload-hash-mismatch
cases.note: the recomputed payload hash differs from the claimed one

cases.name: valid-revision-conflict
cases.note: the retriable case, carrying currentRevision so the retry costs one round trip

cases.name: valid-idempotency-conflict
cases.note: commandId identifies which in-flight id collided; not retriable

cases.name: valid-illegal-transition
cases.note: the command type is not legal from the current state; currentState says what is

cases.name: valid-deadline-exceeded
cases.note: the platform window elapsed; the deadline edge, not this command, governs

cases.name: valid-evidence-not-validated
cases.note: the cited evidence is missing or failed intake validation

cases.name: valid-funding-not-final
cases.note: funding is broadcast but not final; retry after the stated delay

cases.name: valid-rate-limited
cases.note: a caller-level limit, carrying the delay a client MUST honour

cases.name: valid-internal-error
cases.note: transient Runtime failure; retry idempotently under the same commandId

cases.name: reject-unknown-code
cases.note: codes are enumerated: an unhandled branch fails as a schema error

cases.name: reject-retriable-contradicts-catalog
cases.note: schema-valid but semantically wrong — retriable disagrees with the catalog, caught by the cross-check rather than the schema

cases.name: reject-missing-retriable
cases.note: retriable is required on the wire, not inferred from a vendored catalog
